domain: EU food-safety zoonoses reporting - EFSA EU One Health Zoonoses Report sample-based prevalence data (EU agency publisher; per-country submissions on Zenodo)
prediction_question: Would be: for a food/animal sample drawn under national zoonoses monitoring in a reporting country, will it test positive for a stated pathogen, given sampling-plan attributes - the EU-wide twin of the task this bench already carries as bvl-zoom-sample-positivity (investigating, verdict go). See rejection_reason: the task is not a discovery today.
prediction_time: Would be the moment the sample is taken (all features are sampling-plan/item attributes); annual publication ~1 year after the reporting year (measured: the 2024 reporting-year records published 2025-12-09). Not pinned further - rejected before probing the data.
target_definition: Would be the qualitative detection result per (sample, parameter) row - the same label family as bvl-zoom-sample-positivity's ErgAlphaT. Not pinned this session; see rejection_reason.

sources.name: EFSA - 'Sample based prevalence data complementing the European Union One Health Zoonoses Report' (per-country, per-reporting-year records on Zenodo)
sources.api: measured 2026-10-22 via the Zenodo API (anonymous, tokenless): 36 records total, one per (reporting country x reporting year) - e.g. 2024 reporting year: Finland (Zenodo 17699315, SAMPLE_PREV_2024_FI.CSV, 1,707,164 B), Germany (17699448, SAMPLE_PREV_2024_DE.zip, 5,870,868 B), Croatia (17699515, 2,408,502 B), Ireland (17700174, 25,576 B), Sweden (17700657, 28,278 B), Norway (17700602, 32,249 B), the United Kingdom/XI (17701722, 25,874 B); 2023 reporting year: Finland (14016429, PRV_SSD2_2023_FI.ZIP, 152,778 B), Ireland (14016555, 24,771 B), Luxembourg (17700544, 528,355 B) - published 2024-12-10 / 2025-12-09, i.e. roughly a one-year publication lag. Sample-level rows in EFSA's SSD2 format (the same stream the German BVL publishes nationally as ZooM open data; the bvl-zoom record already notes its data are 'the German contribution to EFSA's EU-wide zoonoses reporting').
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 on every record probed (license id cc-by-4.0 read from the Zenodo API metadata, 2026-10-22) - class A.
sources.access: anonymous direct downloads from Zenodo, tokenless; the data itself is excellent and fully usable - this is a task-novelty rejection, not an access or licence rejection.

measurements.zenodo_series_2026_10_22: Zenodo API title search 'Sample based prevalence data' AND zoonoses -> 36 records, per (country x reporting year), all cc-by-4.0; 2024-year records published 2025-12-09 (~1-year lag); file sizes from 25 KB (IE) to 5.9 MB (DE).
measurements.coverage_note_2026_10_22: The series is the EU-wide sample-level zoonoses stream (SSD2 format) that national programmes feed; Germany's member of this series is the same stream bvl-zoom-sample-positivity is built on (BVL ZooM open data, dl-de/by-2.0).

rejection_reason: Rejected as a task-shape duplicate of a candidate already open on this bench. The sample-level pathogen-positivity prediction task on this exact reporting stream IS bvl-zoom-sample-positivity (status investigating, verdict go, opened 2026-10-21): same grain (sample x parameter), same label family (qualitative detection result), same timing (attributes decided at sampling), and - measured then - the German ZooM data are the German contribution to this same EU One Health reporting. Building the EU-wide version now would be a second instance of a candidate the bench has not yet constructed once, which the project's novelty rule names as not a discovery ('repeating a task on a different source'). The data quality verdict is recorded for the future: licence class A (CC BY 4.0), anonymous access, per-country per-year records all pinned in this record's sources - so IF bvl-zoom is constructed, qualified and published, and a multi-instance extension is then wanted, this rejection names exactly where the EU-wide files live. Open a FRESH candidate for that extension at that time; do not reopen this record.
next_action: Terminal for now. If and only if bvl-zoom-sample-positivity reaches publication and a second geographic instance is wanted, open a fresh candidate on these Zenodo records (the 36 record ids and file sizes are pinned in sources above); until then the EU-wide sample-positivity task stays closed.

jurisdiction.publisher: European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), an EU agency headquartered in Parma, Italy - the EU One Health Zoonoses Report series; the records are national submissions published on Zenodo
jurisdiction.convention: EU agency publisher; 'EU' recorded as the country per the same convention as ecdc-atlas-surveillance. The data describe 30+ reporting countries incl. EEA non-EU (NO) and the UK (XI).

licence_note: CC BY 4.0 on every probed Zenodo record; licence is not the rejection reason (task novelty is)
